title: How to choose safe investments for short-term savings goals in the US
description: Matching the vehicle to the timeline: 1 year, 3 years, and 5 years.
content:
Saving for a wedding in 12 months is different than saving for retirement in 30 years. When the goal is short-term, the priority shifts from 'Growth' to 'Preservation'. You cannot afford for the stock market to drop 20% right before you need to pay the venue. However, leaving money in a 0% checking account loses to inflation. The goal is to find the highest 'Risk-Free' yield available. This guide maps specific US investment vehicles to your time horizon.

Key Takeaways

  • Duration Matching: Match the asset's maturity to your goal date. If the goal is in 6 months, buy a 6-month T-Bill.
  • No Stocks: If the timeline is < 3 years, stocks are gambling. The market can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent.
  • State Taxes: In high-tax states (CA/NY), Treasury Bills beat CDs because the interest is state-tax free.
  • Liquidity vs Yield: CDs pay more but lock your money. HYSAs pay less but offer instant access. Choose based on certainty of the expense.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Current US interest rates (2025) offer a 'free lunch' for savers. You can earn ~4-5% with zero risk. This is historically anomalous. Take advantage of it for your short-term buckets.

The Safety Menu

Where to put the money.

0-12 Months (Liquid)

Vehicle: High-Yield Savings Account (HYSA) or Money Market Fund (VMFXX).

Why: You might need the cash tomorrow. Rates are variable, but liquidity is 100%. No penalties.

1-2 Years (Locked)

Vehicle: Treasury Bills or CDs.

Why: You lock in the rate. If the Fed cuts rates next month, your 1-Year CD still pays the old high rate. You eliminate 'Reinvestment Risk'.

3-5 Years (Inflation Protected)

Vehicle: Series I Savings Bonds or Short-Term Bond Funds (BSV).

Why: I-Bonds track inflation. Bond funds offer slightly higher potential return but have small price volatility. Acceptable risk for a 4-year timeline.

Execution Tactics

  1. The 'Ladder' Strategy: If saving for a house in 'about a year', buy a 3-month T-Bill every month. You constantly have money maturing, but earn higher rates than savings.
  2. Avoid Corporate Bonds: For short-term safety, avoid corporate debt. Even safe companies can have credit events. Stick to US Government or FDIC Insured Paper.
  3. Automate the Exit: Set a calendar alert 1 month before your goal date. 'Sell T-Bills / Transfer to Checking'. Don't wait until the invoice arrives to liquefy assets.

Frequently Asked Questions

What about a 'Stablecoin'?

No. Stablecoins have counterparty risk (the issuer could fail). US Treasuries have no counterparty risk (the US Gov prints the money). For safety, choose the Gov.

Can I use a CD for an emergency fund?

No. Penalties for early withdrawal defeat the purpose. Keep the E-Fund in HYSA. Keep the 'Planned Spend' (wedding) in CDs.

How do I buy T-Bills?

Fidelity or Schwab. Search 'Fixed Income -> New Issues'. It is commission-free and easier to manage than TreasuryDirect.
